analysis: Integration of three source-pass analyses; no findings. The only runtime change is console-ui/src/lib/chat/stream.ts (head ~226-235). After optional unsealing and JSON parse, a top-level `error` event is now terminal. It dispatches the promotion-usage event, calls onError with `Stream failed: <message>` and returns without onDone or later deltas. The sealed-stream decrypt failure path is unchanged and still fails closed (TB-001, A-001, T-003). The error message is attacker-influenceable (provider or coordinator, ADV-001), but a provider can already terminate or corrupt its own stream, so this is no new capability. Stopping content delivery after an error reduces the risk of failed output being shown as complete. Residual: XSS depends on how the downstream UI (useChatStream and the components that render the error) renders the string. That code was not supplied. React text rendering is likely safe, and the risk is pre-existing in kind (T-019 context). The other changes are a changelog, docs, test fixtures (fake account_id/stripe_account_id values; tweetnacl keys generated at test time) and docs/architecture/components/console-ui.md. The docs file was supplied as text with no visible diff, so changed statements could not be identified. It describes the server-only coordinator URL (T-017), mock auth (T-020), CSP with unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval, and GA consent defaulting to granted; these are disclosed existing behaviors. No attestation, App Attest, billing, or provider-trust code changed, so TB-009 and TB-011 are unaffected. Coverage limit: landing/ routes described in the docs (proxy inference, provider-stories webhook) were not supplied, and the UI rendering of the stream error was not verified.
